input.quote: Any disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with the then-current commercial arbitration rules of the American Arbitration Association ("RULES"). The arbitration shall be conducted by one (1) arbitrator appointed in accordance with the Rules in San Francisco County, California.
input.rationale: Governing law is California, which is within the accepted list (and appropriate here as both parties are California-based), so the choice of law is compliant. However, the clause imposes mandatory single-arbitrator AAA arbitration rather than resolution in court, which deviates from the playbook requirement for courts as the dispute forum. The arbitration seat is domestic (San Francisco), so this is not a walk-away issue. We took the fallback (California law and courts) rather than pushing New York, since the California-law bargain is reasonable for these parties; the minimal edit swaps the arbitration forum for exclusive jurisdiction of the San Francisco state and federal courts and conforms the heading.

proposal.summary: Replace mandatory AAA arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of California state and federal courts; retain California governing law.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have replaced mandatory AAA arbitration with the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in San Francisco County, retaining California law, because our position is that disputes be resolved in court rather than by binding arbitration. Our preferred position is New York law and the courts of New York County, but California courts are acceptable here given both parties are California-based.

ops.oldText: Any disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with the then-current commercial arbitration rules of the American Arbitration Association ("RULES"). The arbitration shall be conducted by one (1) arbitrator appointed in accordance with the Rules in San Francisco County, California. A judgment upon the award may be entered in any court having jurisdiction of the parties, including without limitation the courts in San Francisco, California. The non-prevailing party in the arbitration shall pay all fees and charges of the American Arbitration Association; each party, however, shall be responsible for the payment of all fees and expenses connected with the presentation of its respective case.
ops.newText: Any disputes arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively in the state and federal courts located in San Francisco County, California, and each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of those courts and waives any objection to venue or inconvenient forum therein.
